# Required status checks, per protected branch (GitHub branch protection).
#
# ONE home for the lists. FOUR readers — and only one of them parses this file:
#   scripts/ci/required-checks.py           the parser (@all / @<branch> selection)
#   scripts/ci/apply-branch-protection.sh   PUTs a branch's set to GitHub (admin token)
#   scripts/ci/test-changed-modules.py      asserts every name exists as a check-run AND
#                                           that its workflow starts PRs on that branch
#   scripts/ci/release-gates.py             waits on these names before any deploy
# Listing a check here changes nothing on GitHub until someone runs the apply script for
# that branch. That gap is how this file and `main`'s live protection drifted apart
# (AUD-TEST-003: "main merges previously ran with no required gate at all").
#
# FORMAT
#   "@all" or "@<branch>" opens a section; every bare line under it is a required context
#   for that branch. A branch's set is @all plus its own @<branch> section. Blank lines
#   and "#" comments are ignored; a malformed "@" directive is an error, not a skipped
#   line — a typo'd header would otherwise swallow every check under it and silently
#   un-gate the branch.
#
#   The @<branch> sections ARE the declaration of which branches this repo gates:
#   test-changed-modules.py validates every context against the triggers of the branch
#   named above it, and apply-branch-protection.sh refuses to run for a branch with no
#   section. To gate a new branch, add its section; to retire one, delete it.
#
# WHY PER-BRANCH (measured 2026-11-17)
#   The candidate sets come from two workflows with different triggers, so they are not
#   interchangeable and must not be flattened into one list:
#     ci.yml            "CI — CLAUDE.md gates"          push + pull_request -> [main]
#     ci-optimized.yml  "CI (Zero-Billing Optimized)"   push + pull_request -> [main]
#   @all exists for the day a second branch is gated again: a context that only reports
#   on some branches does not belong under @all, and the test fails if you put one there.
#
# These are CHECK-RUN names, not workflow names — you cannot require "ci.yml".
# For a job that calls a reusable workflow the name is "<caller job name> / <job id
# inside the reusable>"; for an inline job it is the job's `name:`, and `name:` is
# OPTIONAL — an unnamed job reports its bare job id (all five ci-optimized contexts are
# ids like "secrets-scan", which is why a validator that greps only `name:` lines cannot
# see them, and why it must not credit a bare id to a job that DOES set a name: ci.yml's
# `backend` job reports as "backend (go build + vet)", so treating the id as a second
# name there would let a main-only context pass as develop-safe).
#
# ⚠️ RENAMING A JOB HERE BREAKS EVERY PR AND EVERY DEPLOY. Branch protection matches on
# the exact string, and release-gates.py waits on it too; the old context simply never
# reports again, so PRs sit forever on "Expected — waiting for status" and a release
# stalls to `timeout`. That is why test-changed-modules.py asserts every name below still
# exists as a job — rename a job and CI fails loudly instead of merges and deploys
# hanging silently.
#
# Only UNCONDITIONAL jobs belong here. Module lanes are gated on the router and report
# "skipped" when their module did not change; GitHub does treat a skipped check as
# satisfied, but requiring them couples branch protection to routing for no gain — a lane
# that must run already runs.
#
# To change the set: edit this file, then
#   python3 scripts/ci/test-changed-modules.py
#   python3 scripts/ci/test-release-gates.py
#   python3 scripts/ci/required-checks.py --branch main      # preview; writes nothing
# then re-apply protection for each gated branch (admin token):
#   GITHUB_TOKEN=<admin token> scripts/ci/apply-branch-protection.sh main

# Everything `main` requires: both gate sets. The first nine are ci.yml's unconditional
# jobs; the last five are ci-optimized.yml's, which is what `main` is protected by today.
# Keeping both here is what lets the apply script be run for `main` without dropping the
# secrets gate — the old flat list silently did exactly that.
@main
backend (go build + vet) / verify
frontend-admin (type-check) / typecheck
frontend-web (regression + money + contract + tsc + lint) / verify
hygiene (client secrets + live-DB test gate + migration versions)
migrations (additive-only guard) / guard
mobile (whole-app tsc) / typecheck
openapi (validate all contracts) / validate
which modules changed
workflows (actionlint)
backend
frontend-admin
frontend-web
migrations
secrets-scan

# develop is deliberately NOT declared. ci.yml removed develop/staging/prod from both its
# triggers ("releases come from main alone"), so no ci.yml or ci-optimized.yml check-run
# can ever report for a PR whose base is develop — requiring the nine names there, as
# GitHub's protection for `develop` still does, leaves such a PR stuck on "Expected"
# forever. Clearing or re-scoping develop's live protection is an admin action, not a
# repo edit; see docs/launch/BRANCH-PROTECTION.md.
